review_notes: I read the whole file. I also checked the Mathlib Path homotopy API (`Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Path.lean`: `eval`, `eval_zero`, `eval_one`) and the uses of `Homotopy.reparam` in `FundamentalGroupoid/Basic.lean`. The simp lemmas are `reparamHomotopy_apply`, `prepend_apply`, `prependHomotopyEquiv_apply` and `prependHomotopyEquiv_symm_apply`. All four are `rfl` lemmas that unfold a newly defined bundled map to a standard form (`Path.trans`, `Homotopy.eval`). None of them overlaps with another rule, and none can loop. The `by simp` proofs in `reparamHomotopy` close through Mathlib's existing `eval_zero` and `eval_one`. I found no missing canonical simp lemma, wrong orientation, competing rules or cycle that I could support with evidence. One residual uncertainty: `reparamHomotopy_apply` rewrites to `(Homotopy.reparam ..).eval s`, which has no further simp lemmas. I could not show that this expansion hurts any use. I did not run Lean.
